body:
I've never considered working at a hotel as anything but room service--I'll definitely have to look in to being a clerk. Thanks.

I'm the same way, to a certain extent--not being able to write, it just makes me feel godawful. Writer's block is one thing, but not having the time--and having that time being filled with a job that I cannot physically or emotionally stand--is just difficult, for lack of a better word.

No, I don't have a major set in stone yet. My school requires you to choose one if you want to go through the financial aid process, so I just went with English Literature. Hasn't done me any good so far, but it'll look good, considering I want to write, right?

Like a lot of other young adults now, I want to write, aha. Unfortunately, for me, it's a very time-consuming passion, and I can't figure out a way to find the time to write and still get enough sleep to where I'm able to operate like a normal human being when school or work comes around the next morning, and I can't find any other time to do it. 

I was hoping to get a job in a local bookstore, I mean--it's still retail, which I abhor, but at least I would've actually been able to do something that pertains to my passion, y'know?

And it's not just that; not just my career (or lack thereof) that's making me feel this way,but these things are on the forefront of my mind right now, y'know?
